import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1113

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial
  Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
- [Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe,
  Warsaw (1960).
- [FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers,
  Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.

A positive odd integer $k$ is a *Sierpiński number* if $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is composite for all
$n \geq 0$. A *covering set* for $k$ is a finite set of primes $P$ such that every number of
the form $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is divisible by at least one prime in $P$.

Sierpiński (1960) proved that infinitely many Sierpiński numbers exist using covering systems.
The smallest known Sierpiński number is 78557 (Selfridge). Erdős and Graham conjectured that
there exist Sierpiński numbers with no finite covering set. A negative answer would imply
infinitely many Fermat primes.

Note: The notion of a covering set for a Sierpiński number is closely related to a
`CoveringSystem` of $\mathbb{Z}$ (see
`FormalConjecturesForMathlib.NumberTheory.CoveringSystem`): a finite covering set of primes
for $k$ works because the exponents $n$ for which each prime divides $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ form
residue classes whose union covers all of $\mathbb{Z}$, i.e. a covering system.

See also Erdős Problems [203](https://www.erdosproblems.com/203) and
[276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276).
-/

namespace Erdos1113

/--
A *covering set* for a positive odd integer $k$ is a finite set of primes $P$ such that every
number of the form $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is divisible by at least one prime in $P$.
-/
def HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ ∀ n, ∃ p ∈ P, p ∣ (k * 2 ^ n + 1)

/--
Sierpiński [Si60] proved that there are infinitely many Sierpiński numbers, using covering
systems to construct suitable covering sets for any $k$ satisfying a certain congruence.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P1113.lean#L22"]
theorem erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski :
    Set.Infinite {k : ℕ | k.IsSierpinskiNumber} := by
  sorry

/--
**Erdős Problem 1113.** Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] conjectured that the answer is yes. A negative answer would imply
that there are infinitely many Fermat primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ ¬ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

/--
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek :
    ∀ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber →
      k.IsPerfectPower ∨ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

end Erdos1113

findings.description: The bibliography at lines 26–27 identifies [Si60] as Sierpiński's Elementary Theory of Numbers, Warsaw (1960). The 1960 source of the infinitude theorem is instead his article “Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n + 1.” The English book Elementary Theory of Numbers dates to 1964. This reference error does not affect any Lean statement.
findings.source_evidence: Sierpiński's original article, Elemente der Mathematik 15 (1960), pp. 73–74, explicitly states the infinitude theorem on p. 73: https://doi.org/10.5169/seals-20713. FFK08 likewise cites this article as reference [12]. The publications section at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wac%C5%82aw_Sierpi%C5%84ski dates the English book to 1964.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [Si60] with: Sierpiński, W., Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n + 1, Elemente der Mathematik 15 (1960), 73–74, DOI 10.5169/seals-20713.

reformulations.difference: ErGr80, p. 27, asks whether every eligible odd integer has a positive integer N sharing a nontrivial factor with every positive-exponent term, and conjectures a negative answer. Lean asks positively for a counterexample and expresses covering through a finite set of primes.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The conjectured failure of universal covering is exactly existence of a Sierpiński number without a covering. A finite prime cover P gives N = ∏ p∈P, p; conversely, the prime divisors of N form a finite cover when every gcd is greater than 1. Positive versus nonnegative exponents causes no change: a Sierpiński number is odd and greater than 1, so k+1 is composite; a positive-exponent cover can be extended to exponent 0 by adjoining 2. The complete equivalence with the negated universal gcd formulation was proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean as Review1113.main_reformulation. Thus a positive answer in Lean corresponds to the negative answer conjectured in the book.

reformulations.difference: FFK08 Conjecture 3 says that a Sierpiński number not of the form ℓ^r, with ℓ ≥ 1 and r > 1, has its smallest prime divisor of k·2^n+1 bounded as n tends to infinity. Lean instead states the disjunction 'perfect power or finite prime cover,' using nonnegative exponents and a perfect-power base greater than 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite prime cover bounds the least prime divisor by its largest member. Conversely, a bound gives a cover consisting of the primes below that bound; an eventual bound becomes a uniform bound by absorbing finitely many initial terms. The conditional on non-perfect-powers is classically equivalent to the stated disjunction. Allowing base 1 does not matter because a Sierpiński number exceeds 1, and the exponent-0 convention is harmless as above. The full equivalence was kernel-checked as Review1113.ffk_reformulation in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

sources_consulted: Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), §3, especially p. 27: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
Sierpiński, Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n + 1, Elemente der Mathematik 15 (1960), 73–74: https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=edm-001%3A1960%3A15%3A%3A132&bot=1

Filaseta–Finch–Kozek, On Powers Associated with Sierpiński Numbers, Riesel Numbers and Polignac's Conjecture, especially §2, Conjecture 3, and reference [12]: https://people.math.sc.edu/filaseta/papers/SierpinskiEtCoPapNew.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the definition or three theorems. Boundary checks exclude k = 0 and k = 1 and an empty covering set; small perfect-power cases and Selfridge's 36-residue covering were tested. The cited infinitude proof has matching definitions and statement and kernel-checks with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound after moving its introductory module docstring below the import. The live erdosproblems.com pages returned Cloudflare 403 responses despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the mathematics was checked against the primary literature, and the current independent database records problem 1113 as open. Experiments are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file is unchanged.
